_note: Orbit/physical values are game-scaled, not real. Lore is original wording; expand trivia yourself. Put this file at src/data/planets.json.

asteroidBelt._note: Static belt between Giedi Prime's aphelion (~10,260) and Kaitain's perihelion (~12,250).

lore.title: The Sun of Arrakis
lore.summary: The star that Arrakis orbits. In the game it anchors the whole system.
trivia: In the books, Arrakis is the third planet of this star.

pointsOfInterest.name: Abandoned Harvester
pointsOfInterest.description: A spice harvester half swallowed by the sand. Its crew left in a hurry when something large moved beneath them.

pointsOfInterest.name: Thumper
pointsOfInterest.description: A spring-driven stake beating the sand in a steady rhythm. Someone planted it to lure a sandworm away from somewhere else.

pointsOfInterest.name: Sietch Doorway
pointsOfInterest.description: A seal cut into the rock, hiding the way into a cave settlement. Whoever lives inside does not want visitors.

lore.title: The Desert Planet
lore.summary: A world of endless sand with almost no surface water. It is the only known source of the spice, which makes it the most valuable planet in the empire.
trivia: Giant sandworms roam beneath the dunes and are drawn to rhythmic vibration.
Its native desert people, the Fremen, survive by recycling nearly every drop of water.
Control of Arrakis means control of the spice trade, so great houses fight over it.

pointsOfInterest.name: Fishing Buoy
pointsOfInterest.description: A marker for the fishing fleets, still blinking long after the boats moved on.

pointsOfInterest.name: Sea-cliff Watchtower
pointsOfInterest.description: A weathered stone tower from the long Atreides rule, built to watch for storms and ships.

lore.title: The Ocean World
lore.summary: A green, wet planet of seas and cliffs. It was the ancestral home of House Atreides before they moved to Arrakis.
trivia: House Atreides ruled this sea world for many generations before the Emperor ordered them to take over Arrakis.
Its wealth came from the sea and from pundi rice grown in flooded paddies along the coasts.
Duke Leto's father, the Old Duke, was killed in Caladan's bullring by the bull he was fighting.

pointsOfInterest.name: Slag Obelisk
pointsOfInterest.description: A column of cast industrial waste, raised as a monument to production quotas.

pointsOfInterest.name: Gutted Ornithopter
pointsOfInterest.description: A Harkonnen patrol craft stripped for parts. Nothing on this world is allowed to go to waste.

pointsOfInterest.name: Fighting Pit
pointsOfInterest.description: The remains of an arena where captives were made to fight for an audience.

lore.title: The Harkonnen Homeworld
lore.summary: A dark, heavily industrialised world ruled by House Harkonnen, the bitter rivals of House Atreides.
trivia: Baron Vladimir Harkonnen rules it from a fortress city and plots the ruin of House Atreides.
Its people live under fear, slavery and surveillance; the planet's industry runs on forced labour.
The Harkonnens controlled Arrakis and its spice harvest for decades before the Atreides were given the fief.

pointsOfInterest.name: Imperial Obelisk
pointsOfInterest.description: A polished marker bearing the Corrino lion, set where the Emperor's gardens begin.

pointsOfInterest.name: Garden Colonnade
pointsOfInterest.description: Columns from an older palace wing, kept as a picturesque ruin by the court's gardeners.

lore.title: The Imperial Capital
lore.summary: Seat of the Padishah Emperor and House Corrino, the political centre of the empire.
trivia: The Padishah Emperor Shaddam IV of House Corrino holds court here.
Its gardens, palaces and carefully managed climate are a showcase of imperial wealth.
Princess Irulan, the Emperor's eldest daughter and later a historian of these events, was raised at this court.

pointsOfInterest.name: Prison Camp Remains
pointsOfInterest.description: Broken walls of a labour camp. Those who survive places like this are taken to become the Emperor's soldiers.

pointsOfInterest.name: Crashed Transport
pointsOfInterest.description: A prisoner transport that never reached its landing field.

pointsOfInterest.name: Scorched Spire
pointsOfInterest.description: Rock fused to glass by the ancient attack that ruined this world.

lore.title: The Prison Planet
lore.summary: A harsh, devastated world used as the empire's prison. Its brutal conditions forged the emperor's elite soldiers.
trivia: It was once the imperial capital, until a devastating attack long ago left it a ruined, hostile world.
The Emperor's feared Sardaukar soldiers are recruited from the survivors of its prison camps.
How the Sardaukar are trained here is one of House Corrino's most closely guarded secrets.

pointsOfInterest.name: Sealed Shaft Cap
pointsOfInterest.description: A plain metal hatch flush with the ground. Somewhere beneath it, a city works in secret.

pointsOfInterest.name: Survey Beacon
pointsOfInterest.description: An Ixian marker broadcasting on a band no other house can read.

lore.title: The Machine World
lore.summary: A planet famous for its advanced technology, with much of its industry hidden underground.
trivia: Ixian engineers build machines that go right up to the limit set by the old ban on thinking machines.
Most of its cities and factories are hidden underground, so the surface looks almost untouched.
The Great Houses buy Ixian technology even while they distrust where its inventions might lead.

lore.title: Uncharted Anomaly
lore.summary: Not part of Dune canon. An original addition: a black hole at the edge of the system whose gravity bends starlight around it.
trivia: Light passing close to it is bent so strongly that stars behind it appear as a ring.
